# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 39 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 39 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_039_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Notes

Mandate 6 introduces the Two Angel doctrine, a motif also found in the Qumran Community Rule (1QS 3-4) and the Didache (1:1). Hermas's formulation is distinctive: the two angels are not cosmic forces but personal attendants who work from within the human heart. The Greek *dipsychos* ("double-minded") underlies the entire Mandate sequence; the person who cannot distinguish the two angels is prey to double-mindedness.

Key terms: *aggelos dikaiosynes* (angel of righteousness) and *aggelos tes ponērias* (angel of wickedness). The angel of righteousness is described as *leptos* (delicate/tender/gentle) — an unusual word choice that EMET preserves as "delicate" and LOGOS renders "tender." SOPHIA prefers "tender" as it better conveys moral sensitivity. *Oxycholos* (quick-tempered/wrathful) is the dominant characteristic of the evil angel. The vice list in 39:5 is one of the longest in Hermas and reflects standard Hellenistic-Jewish ethical catalogues.

---

## Mandate 6, Part 1 — On the Two Angels

**39:1** "In the first commandment," he said, "I charged you to keep faith, fear, and self-control." "Yes, lord," I replied. "Now," he said, "I wish to make known to you the powers of these commandments, so that you may understand what power each possesses and what it works."

**39:2** "Two angels attend upon every person," he said — "one of righteousness and one of wickedness." "How then, lord," I asked, "shall I recognize their workings, since both dwell with me?"

**39:3** "Hear and understand them," he said. "The angel of righteousness is tender, modest, gentle, and tranquil. When he arises in your heart, he speaks with you immediately concerning righteousness, purity, holiness, self-control, and every righteous deed and every glorious virtue. When all these things arise in your heart, know that the angel of righteousness is with you. These are the works of the angel of righteousness. Trust him therefore and his works."

**39:4** "Now look also at the works of the angel of wickedness. First, he is quick-tempered, bitter, and senseless, and his works are evil and overturn the servants of God. When he arises in your heart, know him by his works."

**39:5** "How I shall recognize him, lord, I do not know," I said. "Listen," he said. "When a fit of anger or bitterness comes upon you, know that he is in you. And likewise the craving for many transactions, the extravagance of rich foods and drunken excess, diverse and needless pleasures, desire for women, avarice, overweening pride and boastfulness, and all things like and akin to these — when these things arise in your heart, know that the angel of wickedness is in you."

**39:6** "Since you know his works, withdraw from him and trust him not at all, for his works are evil and harmful to the servants of God. You have before you the works of both angels. Understand them and trust the angel of righteousness."

---

*SOPHIA represents the consensus rendering of EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA, with rulings recorded in the Disagreement Log.*
